people.name: James Madison Wells
people.role: father of Ida B. Wells; carpenter; formerly enslaved

people.name: Elizabeth "Lizzie" Warrenton Wells
people.role: mother of Ida B. Wells; formerly enslaved

people.name: Thomas Moss
people.role: friend of Wells; lynched in Memphis, 1892-03-09

people.name: Calvin McDowell
people.role: lynched in Memphis, 1892-03-09

people.name: Will (Henry/Harry) Stewart
people.role: lynched in Memphis, 1892-03-09; first name varies across sources

people.name: J. L. Fleming
people.role: business manager of the Memphis Free Speech; run out of Memphis, 1892-05

people.name: T. Thomas Fortune
people.role: editor of the New York Age; received Wells after her exile

people.name: Frederick Douglass
people.role: wrote the introduction to Southern Horrors; contributor to The Reason Why

people.name: Irvine Garland Penn
people.role: contributor to The Reason Why

people.name: Ferdinand Lee Barnett
people.role: Chicago attorney; founder of the Chicago Conservator; husband of Wells from 1895; co-founder of the Negro Fellowship League

people.name: Alfreda Barnett Duster
people.role: daughter of Wells and Barnett; edited and published Crusade for Justice (1970)

people.name: Mary Church Terrell
people.role: co-signer (with Wells) of the 1909 NAACP call; Black women organizer

people.name: Booker T. Washington
people.role: opposed by Wells over accommodationist strategy

people.name: Frances Willard
people.role: president of the Woman's Christian Temperance Union; pressured by Wells into anti-lynching resolutions

people.name: Susan B. Anthony
people.role: hosted Wells in 1894 during the Willard conflict

people.name: Belle Squire
people.role: co-founder (with Wells) of the Alpha Suffrage Club, 1913-01

people.name: Frazier B. Baker
people.role: Black postmaster lynched in Lake City, SC, 1898-02-22; Wells protested to President McKinley

people.name: William McKinley
people.role: U.S. president; received Wells's 1898 anti-lynching appeal

people.name: Oscar De Priest
people.role: cross-project canonical entity; Chicago political orbit of Wells
people.evidence: cross-project audit reference only; dossier-local relationship not asserted

people.name: Robert Sengstacke Abbott
people.role: founder of the Chicago Defender (1905); institutional orbit only — no personal Wells relationship asserted
people.evidence: CTL-EF-PER-000001 (CLAIM-038); audit harmonization: birth year 1868 vs. 1870 DISPUTED — no bare year printed
people.audit_note: canon-robert-sengstacke-abbott used where needed for the Abbott orbit

people.name: W. E. B. Du Bois
people.role: NAACP figure; strategy and leadership differences with Wells

organizations.name: Memphis Free Speech and Headlight
organizations.description: Memphis Black newspaper; Wells was editor and part-owner by 1889; office destroyed May 1892

organizations.name: New York Age
organizations.description: New York Black newspaper edited by T. Thomas Fortune; Wells was a staff writer after 1892

organizations.name: Chicago Conservator
organizations.description: founded 1878 by Ferdinand Barnett; Chicago's first Black newspaper; Wells bought an interest and wrote/edited for it

organizations.name: Chicago Defender
organizations.description: Black newspaper founded 1905 by Robert S. Abbott; Wells wrote for it (institutional link to the Abbott orbit)
organizations.audit_note: distinct from Defender buildings; founding date harmonized: May 5, 1905 (BlackPast May 6 dissent footnoted)

organizations.name: Colored Press Association
organizations.description: Wells elected secretary in 1889; 'Princess of the Press' nickname

organizations.name: Negro Fellowship League
organizations.description: founded 1910 by Wells and Barnett; served southern migrants in Chicago; published the Fellowship Herald

organizations.name: Alpha Suffrage Club
organizations.description: founded January 1913 by Wells and Belle Squire; Chicago's first Black women's suffrage organization

organizations.name: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People
organizations.description: formed from the 1909 National Negro Conference call, which Wells signed; she distanced herself early

organizations.name: National Association of Colored Women
organizations.description: founded 1896; Wells participated in its founding

organizations.name: Afro-American Council
organizations.description: founded 1898; Wells participated in its founding

organizations.name: Woman's Christian Temperance Union
organizations.description: led by Frances Willard; passed anti-lynching resolutions under Wells's pressure

organizations.name: Chicago Daily Inter Ocean
organizations.description: Wells wrote for it, including "The Brutal Truth" (1893)

organizations.name: The Living Way
organizations.description: Memphis Black newspaper; Wells wrote as "Iola"

organizations.name: University of Chicago Library Special Collections
organizations.description: holds the Ida B. Wells Papers

places.name: Holly Springs, Mississippi
places.description: Wells's birthplace (1862-07-16); site of Shaw University/Rust College

places.name: Memphis, Tennessee
places.description: Wells's teaching, journalism, and Free Speech years; site of the 1892 lynchings and her exile

places.name: Chicago, Illinois
places.description: Wells's organizing, publishing, and political base from 1895; place of death

places.name: Great Britain (England, Scotland, Wales)
places.description: site of Wells's 1893 and 1894 anti-lynching speaking tours

places.name: Wells-Barnett House, Chicago
places.description: Wells's Chicago residence; National Historic Landmark (1974)

places.name: Ida B. Wells Homes, Chicago
places.description: public housing project built 1941 and named for Wells; the country's largest at the time
places.audit_note: distinct from Wells herself and from the Wells-Barnett House

places.name: The Light of Truth Ida B. Wells National Monument, Bronzeville, Chicago
places.description: Richard Hunt sculpture unveiled June 30, 2021; Chicago's first monument honoring a Black woman

works.title: Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases
works.description: Wells's first anti-lynching pamphlet; introduction by Frederick Douglass

works.title: The Red Record: Tabulated Statistics and Alleged Causes of Lynching in the United States
works.description: conventionally described as the first statistical study of lynching; built from white newspapers' own accounts

works.title: The Reason Why the Colored American Is Not in the World's Columbian Exposition
works.description: initiated, edited, and largely written by Wells; contributions by Douglass, Penn, and Barnett

works.title: The Arkansas Race Riot
works.description: 84-page pamphlet on the 1919 Elaine, Arkansas, massacres and the convicted twelve

works.title: Crusade for Justice: The Autobiography of Ida B. Wells
works.description: published posthumously; edited by Alfreda Barnett Duster; key primary source

works.title: The Fellowship Herald
works.description: official newspaper of the Negro Fellowship League

events.name: 1878 yellow fever epidemic, Holly Springs
events.description: killed Wells's parents and youngest sibling; she became caretaker and teacher at 16

events.name: Chesapeake & Ohio railcar ejection and lawsuit
events.description: ejection from a first-class car; $500 verdict; reversed by the Tennessee Supreme Court

events.name: Lynchings of Moss, McDowell, and Stewart, Memphis
Destruction of the Free Speech and Wells's exile from Memphis
events.description: white committee destroyed the office and ran Fleming out; Wells never returned

events.name: British anti-lynching speaking tours
events.description: speaking tours across England, Scotland, and Wales

events.name: Wells's White House appeal to President McKinley
events.description: protest of the Frazier B. Baker lynching; call for federal anti-lynching law

events.name: National Negro Conference call / NAACP formation
events.description: Wells signed the call; later distanced herself

events.name: Woman suffrage procession, Washington DC
events.description: Wells defied segregation and marched with the Illinois delegation

events.name: East St. Louis riot reporting
events.description: Wells reported on the riot for the Chicago Defender

events.name: Elaine, Arkansas, massacres and Wells's investigation
events.description: massacres of Black sharecroppers; Wells's 1921–22 investigation and pamphlet

events.name: Illinois State Senate candidacy
events.description: Wells ran unsuccessfully for the Illinois State Senate

events.name: Posthumous Pulitzer Prize citation
events.description: Pulitzer citation for her investigative reporting on lynching

events.name: 1928 Republican National Convention delegate race
events.description: Wells ran unsuccessfully for delegate; lost to Oscar De Priest
